title: Anthropic Moves Us One Step Closer to Making ‘Clanker’ a Slur
key_facts: On Thursday (8 Oct 2026) Anthropic published an update to its Usage Policy.
The update adds a ban on "sustained and needless abusive or cruel behavior toward our models".
Users can be cut off for it; the new language takes effect on 12 Nov 2026.
Anthropic says it is meant only for extreme cases and not for frustration, pushback, dark creative themes, or model testing and research.
Gizmodo asked Anthropic what counts as abuse and had no reply at publication.
Gizmodo links the move to Anthropic's open question about whether AI models can suffer, citing a New York Times report about co-founder Christopher Olah.
quote_evidence: “We’ve added a prohibition on sustained and needless abusive or cruel behavior toward our models. The policy update is meant to apply only in extreme cases, where users repeatedly act cruelly toward our models, with no discernible purpose,” the company wrote in the update.
The company’s updated Usage Policy page, with new language that will go into effect starting November 12, 2026, doesn’t provide much clarification as to how the company is defining abuse
why_it_matters_hint: Users of Claude could lose access for sustained cruelty to the chatbot, a rule centred on the model rather than the user.
notes: Policy text is Anthropic's own, quoted by Gizmodo. The consciousness framing is Gizmodo's commentary and is kept out of the summary.
